provenance.sha_blocker: GitHub HTML fallback exposed branch/path/content but no full commit permalink; api.github.com DNS/API was unavailable.

target.definition: At least 10,000 deduplicated owner/name candidate project records; document count is not a substitute.

documents.summary: The entry point sends contributors to the community Contributor Guide and requires the Kubernetes CLA before contribution.
The community governance page describes open, welcoming, transparent work and SIG or subproject ownership through charters.
Security contacts direct reporters to the Kubernetes security process and warn against reporting vulnerabilities directly to named contacts.
SIG Release owns release-team coordination, release notes, and versioning processes under its charter.
Kubernetes test-infra provides testing and automation tools, Prow CI, job configuration, local testing, and bot commands.
Prow configuration is a concrete automation source consumed by Kubernetes testing and merge workflows.
Rust directs new contributors to the community channel and development guides, with subtree and source-layout rules for compiler and standard-library work.
The Rust team repository defines team structure and permission synchronization, with membership changes made by pull request.
Rust publishes a dedicated security policy for reporting and handling vulnerabilities.
The Rust release notes document is the project release record and accompanies the stable release process.
Rust CI calculates jobs through src/ci/citool and src/ci/github-actions/jobs.yml, with explicit triggers, permissions, concurrency, and matrices.
The tracking issue template is for accepted features or RFC work and asks for implementation, documentation, and stabilization status.
Django accepts code, documentation, bug reports, and reviews; non-trivial pull requests should begin with a Trac ticket and follow the contribution guide.
Django documents its organization, roles, and project decision structure in the internals guide.
Django provides a dedicated security reporting and handling guide in its official documentation.
Django documents the release process, including release preparation, versioning, and publishing steps.
The tests workflow filters documentation-only changes and runs Django tests across Windows and Ubuntu Python matrices, plus JavaScript and script checks.
The docs workflow has path filters, concurrency and read permissions, then runs documentation lint, formatting, and spelling checks.
Node contribution guidance covers code, documentation, infrastructure, and help, with separate issue and pull request paths under open governance.
Node governance describes triagers, collaborators, and the TSC; triagers can label, comment on, close, and reopen issues.
Node routes security bugs through HackerOne with acknowledgement timelines and OpenJS CNA escalation.
Node release instructions are for TSC-authorized release agents and cover staging, branches, changelog, build, test, tag, signing, promotion, and GitHub release steps.
The benchmark workflow builds Node at the base and merge commits before running benchmark comparisons.
The label workflow runs on pull request events with read-only contents permission and a pinned node-pr-labeler action plus repository configuration.
PyTorch keeps an extensive contribution guide for code, review, development environments, and project-specific contributor workflows.
The PyTorch Foundation page describes the foundation board and points to the project technical governance structure maintained by the community.
PyTorch warns that untrusted models can execute code, recommends isolated environments and provenance or checksums, and gives special caution for torch.load.
PyTorch patch releases require a qualifying regression, triage and Go-No-Go decisions, and a multi-week release process.
The PyTorch CI guide explains GitHub Actions workflows, jobs, runs, matrices, PR versus main behavior, ciflow labels, sharding, and reruns.
The reusable Linux build workflow defines build and test inputs, matrix controls, labels, artifacts, and cloud execution settings.

procedure_cards.title: Read the project entrypoint before implementation
applies_when: starting an external change in a mature project
the repository has a contribution guide or required contributor agreement
counterexamples: an existing maintainer assignment already names the governing procedure
a one-line local experiment is not being proposed upstream
procedure: read CONTRIBUTING and the linked community or developer guide
identify required agreements, issue trackers, labels, tests, and scope limits before editing
keep the change within the documented acceptance path
verification: record the canonical guide URL and confirm the proposed change has a documented issue, ticket, or contributor gate
run the guide-required focused checks before opening a review
recovery: stop if the entrypoint redirects to a different tracker or community guide
ask the project maintainer or community channel which path owns the request

procedure_cards.title: Route work to the documented owner and tracker
applies_when: the project divides work among SIGs, teams, triagers, or a separate issue tracker
a request changes behavior owned by a named subsystem
counterexamples: a documentation typo with no subsystem owner
the project explicitly accepts a change without a tracker or ownership handoff
procedure: map the change to the owning SIG, team, triager group, or tracker
check the owner's labels, design gates, and acceptance criteria
link the implementation or question to that canonical record
verification: the issue or review shows the owner or tracker and the expected label or design state
the proposed files fall within the owner's documented scope
recovery: pause when ownership is ambiguous or a design decision is required
redirect the request to the owner or ask for an explicit maintainer assignment

procedure_cards.title: Keep vulnerability reports on the security path
applies_when: the report may expose an exploitable vulnerability, unsafe model, credential, or sensitive reproduction
counterexamples: an ordinary non-sensitive bug that the project explicitly routes to its public issue tracker
a security policy says the report is out of scope and gives a safer public path
procedure: read the project security policy or contact instructions
use the private reporting channel and include only the information needed for triage
avoid publishing exploit details until the project says disclosure is safe
verification: confirm the private channel and acknowledgement or escalation path from the canonical policy
check that the public issue contains no sensitive reproduction or secret
recovery: if sensitive details were exposed, stop further distribution, follow the project escalation policy, and rotate any exposed credential
if the policy excludes the report, move it to the documented public bug path

procedure_cards.title: Trace CI to its source of truth
applies_when: a change is expected to satisfy repository automation
the project uses generated jobs, reusable workflows, matrices, path filters, or labels
counterexamples: a local script that is not wired into project CI
a documentation-only change excluded by the workflow path filter
procedure: read the trigger and path filters in the workflow
follow references to generated job, matrix, Prow, or reusable-workflow configuration
run the smallest local commands that cover the changed component and record skipped dimensions
verification: map each changed path to a named job or workflow and confirm the local command matches it
separate declared configuration from a remote run result
recovery: if the matrix or job source is unavailable, report the unverified dimension and ask for a maintainer or CI run
rebase or regenerate when the project documents that workflow definitions are merged or generated

procedure_cards.title: Check release authority and rehearse gates
applies_when: preparing a version, tag, package, or published release
the project documents release agents, go-no-go decisions, staging, or signing
counterexamples: a local version bump or changelog draft that is not publishing anything
a maintainer already supplied the project-specific release authorization and dry-run result
procedure: read the release process and identify the authorized role and approval gates
prepare version, changelog, artifacts, and lockfiles in a staging or dry-run path
obtain the documented approval before tag, signing, promotion, or publish
verification: compare the staged artifact, version, changelog, and target commit
after publication, verify the package, tag, release, and checks from the project instructions
recovery: if a partial release exists, inspect package, tag, and release state before retrying
do not repeat an immutable publish until the project owner confirms the recovery path

procedure_cards.title: Treat templates and workflows as contracts
applies_when: opening an issue or PR in a project with a template, labeler, path filter, or reusable workflow
the request depends on a required form field or event trigger
counterexamples: a project explicitly accepts a free-form issue or manual workflow dispatch
the changed path is outside the workflow trigger and should not be expected to run
procedure: inspect required template fields, trigger events, path filters, permissions, and pinned actions
fill the template or adjust scope so the intended check is selected
run the focused local check before relying on the remote workflow
verification: confirm required fields are complete and the changed path matches the intended workflow trigger
record the action or configuration pin when it is part of the contract
recovery: edit the issue or PR to satisfy the template and labels
if the workflow did not trigger, inspect event and path filters before rerunning or asking a maintainer
